During his remarks at a bilateral lunch in Manila with Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Wednesday, Trump praised the country for its seasonal decor.

“And as we can see in the beautiful Christmas decorations and Christmas is such a big part of the Philippines,” Trump said. “I came and I said, ‘Wow, that’s really something. They didn’t talk about taking Christmas away.’”

Then he offered a supposed contrast.

“You know, in our country, they said, ‘Let’s not use Christmas anymore.’ In 2016, we ended that,” Trump claimed. “That was ended. But they treat Christmas with great love and respect in the Philippines.”

No one has been talking about “taking Christmas away” in the United States, nor has anyone seriously suggested not using the term “Christmas” anymore. In fact, the modern supposed war on Christmas is largely a fabrication of right-wing media, which would feign outrage over the use of “happy holidays.”

While some use “happy holidays” to refer to all the holidays of the holiday season and to be more inclusive, the phrase “merry Christmas” has been in constant common use, including by both Democratic and Republican presidents as well as throughout public life by individuals and corporations.

One person who has used “happy holidays,” however, has been Trump himself. He has used it on his greeting cards, on social media, and in his family business. His wife, Melania Trump, is also on the record actively complaining about holiday decor.

“Who gives a fuck about Christmas stuff and decoration?” she said in a 2018 conversation recorded by former friend and aide Stephanie Winston Wolkoff.
